subject: health
unitTitle: Health Literacy and Decision Making in High School
essentialQuestion: How do I turn health information I trust into a decision I can actually defend?

prompts.prompt: Explain what health literacy means at the high-school level in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of internal and external influences on a health decision.
Apply source quality: authorship, evidence, currency, and conflict of interest in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving a repeatable decision process for health choices; correct it and explain why.
Connect short-term convenience versus longer-term consequence with reviewing a decision after the fact without self-blame. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Work a fictional high-school health decision end to end: name the influences, evaluate two competing sources, run the decision process, and state what evidence would change the decision. The learner never has to use a real decision from their own life.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: The decision process may be written, typed, spoken to an adult, diagrammed, recorded on a graphic organizer, or built from sentence stems. A learner may substitute any scenario for another supplied scenario without penalty.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
trustedAdultNote: Direct any urgent safety, health, or mental-health concern to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
